analysis:
The PR changes a single line (410) of docs/reference/configuration.md, the DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK row. It documents that provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/ClusterServiceCommand.swift (`supervisorConfiguration`) now also reads the variable, and that it skips the update check for the `darkbloom cluster` pair at its slot. The change is documentation only, with no code in this batch, so there is no direct regression. I examined the base text at lines 314-675 against the head change. The row sits in the daemon/paths/updates table. No other documented controls changed.

Security relevance: the variable disables auto-update, so it is a local operator knob. It touches T-043 (watchdog and rollback authority), T-013 (binary modification) and T-034 (build qualification). The threat model already treats the operator as ADV-001 with local control, and an operator could always disable updates. Suppressing update checks does not affect attestation or serving authorization (TB-011, A-016, A-017), which are enforced by the coordinator against signed-artifact identity. The documentation does not claim that skipping updates is a trust grant.

Open integration question (outside the supplied evidence): whether the cluster supervisor code honours the variable only from the operator's own environment, and whether skipping updates could leave a cluster pair on a revoked build. A revoked build should still be refused by the coordinator's qualification checks (T-054). The ClusterServiceCommand.swift implementation was not supplied, so I cannot verify it. No finding is warranted from the documentation alone. The cluster pair feature is a separate trust surface, and I did not see its threat-model coverage in the supplied definitions.
